newsitem.title: USA: Mideast donors meet amid fund-wasting scandal.
newsitem.headline: Mideast donors meet amid fund-wasting scandal.

text.p: Countries financing development projects in Palestinian-ruled areas of the West Bank and Gaza Strip held an annual meeting on Thursday amid a row over alleged squandering of Palestinian public funds.
U.S. officials said the one-day meeting of the so-called ad hoc liaison group at the State Department would take stock of aid programmes and no new pledges were expected. Norway chaired the meeting.

The group brings together some 30 countries and international organisations which pledged $2.4 billion to the Palestinians after the 1993 Oslo peace accords with Israel, a figure later expanded to $3.4 billion.

The official Palestinian news agency WAFA said on Thursday that President Yasser Arafat has ordered an inquiry into an auditor's report that members of his administration squandered $326 million in public funds last year.

Palestinians officials say none of the money came from foreign aid but admitted that the affair had caused concern among donors. The Palestinians had already been concerned that disbursement of aid was running behind schedule.
The State Department said earlier this week that the United States could account for "every cent" of the $220 million it has so far given the Palestinians, part of a $500 million, five-year pledge.

"The fact that the Palestinians appear to be policing themselves and identifying publicly some problems in their administration is positive," department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Thursday of the alleged fund-wasting.
